Kleeberg Rules

Build a pyramid together and be the first to get three of your symbols in a straight line.

The basics

Board
The board is a pyramid of fifteen round fields in five rows: one at the top, five at the bottom. One player has the hearts, the other the clovers. The flag marks the top.
Your turn
Put one of your symbols on a free field. You may only build on top of two filled fields: a field is open when both fields directly below it are filled. The bottom row is always open. Open fields are shown with a ring; tap one.
Winning
Whoever first has three of their own symbols in a straight line of neighbouring fields wins. The line can run along a row or down along either slope of the pyramid. The winning line is drawn thick.
Draw
If all fifteen fields are filled and nobody has a line of three, the game is a draw.
Who starts
The player who starts is drawn at the beginning of every game, because moving first is an advantage.
The computer
The computer completes a line when it can. Otherwise it stops your line. Otherwise it avoids opening a field where you could win, and picks any other open field by chance.
Undo
Undo takes back your last move, also against the computer.
